name: agent-view-for-claude-code
description: Spawn, orchestrate, and monitor multiple Claude Code agents — each in its own git worktree — from one panel.

viewsWelcome.contents:
No Claude Code agents found yet.
[New Agent](command:mas.newAgent)
[Open Session Board](command:mas.openCanvas)
[Configure Hooks](command:mas.configureHooks)
Agent View discovers running agents from ~/.claude/projects and can spawn new ones in isolated git worktrees. Open the Session Board to see any session as a board of episodes, plans, commits, and evidence instead of a scroll.

mas.claudePath.description: Path to the Claude Code CLI executable.

mas.defaultModel.description: Model alias passed to spawned agents (e.g. 'opus', 'sonnet'). Empty = Claude Code default.

mas.worktreeRoot.description: Directory (relative to the repo root) where the extension creates per-agent git worktrees.

mas.hookPort.description: Local port the hook server listens on for live Claude Code events.

mas.spawnExtraFlags.description: Extra CLI flags appended to every spawned `claude` invocation.

mas.spawn.planTools.markdownDescription: Give agents Agent View spawns Claude Code's plan tools (`TaskCreate` / `TaskUpdate`) by setting `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1` in their terminal. Current models (Opus 4.8+, Sonnet 5+, Fable) only get these tools when it is set, and plan progress, the Session Board plan and Unattended's stuck-agent nudge all read them. Sessions you start yourself are unaffected.

mas.sessionRegistry.enabled.markdownDescription: Read Claude Code's live session state (`~/.claude/sessions/`, the same source as `claude agents`) for busy / idle / waiting status and the exact thing a session is waiting on. Works without hooks and covers sessions in other windows, the Claude Code extension and background agents. Read-only.

mas.recentDays.description: Only discover sessions whose transcript was modified within this many days (the outer bound).

mas.recentHours.description: Display window: agents idle longer than this are hidden until you use 'Show Older Agents' (active agents always show). Bounded by mas.recentDays.

mas.conflictRadar.enabled.description: Conflict Radar — highlight files edited by more than one agent. Local-only; does NOT use your Claude subscription.

mas.triage.enabled.markdownDescription:
Triage — one inbox for the whole fleet's questions: the same question from different sessions becomes one row, one answer resumes every session waiting on it, and answers become a reusable decision log.

**Off by default.** Turn it on from the Triage panel or **Agent View: Turn On Triage**. Once on, it asks Claude which questions are the same (`mas.triage.ai.enabled`, behind a one-time consent prompt). While off it records nothing and writes nothing.

enumDescriptions: VS Code's private per-workspace storage. Nothing is written into your project.
`.agentview/triage/decisions.json` in the workspace, so the decision log can be committed and shared with your team.
mas.triage.storage.markdownDescription:
Where Triage keeps its decision log.

`internal` (default) writes **nothing into your project** — no files to gitignore.

`repo` writes `.agentview/triage/decisions.json` so your team's recorded decisions travel with the branch. Metric counters stay internal either way, so `repo` adds exactly one file. An existing log is carried over when you switch.

mas.triage.dedup.threshold.description: Lexical similarity above which two questions in the same repo merge without asking Claude. With mas.triage.ai.enabled on this is a fast path, and anything below it down to ~0.35 is adjudicated by Claude; with AI off it is the whole decision.

mas.triage.lookup.threshold.description: Lexical similarity a past decision must reach to auto-answer when Claude is unavailable. With mas.triage.ai.enabled on, every auto-answer is model-confirmed and this is only the offline fallback — deliberately stricter than the dedup threshold.

mas.triage.autoAnswer.enabled.markdownDescription: Answer a question directly from the decision log when a recorded decision matches, covers the question's repo/branch, and hasn't expired. Permission asks and conflicts are never answered this way unless you made the decision on a permission ask itself.

mas.triage.autoAnswer.dryRun.markdownDescription: Log what auto-answer *would* have done, but still ask you. Recommended for the first week. Triage also forces this on by itself if the auto-answer error rate passes 5%.

mas.triage.ai.enabled.markdownDescription:
Let Claude decide whether two agents are asking the same question, and whether a recorded decision really answers a new one. This is what makes Triage work well — token matching cannot tell that "install deps" and "install dependencies" are one decision while "tests for auth" and "tests for billing" are two.

Runs Claude Code in the background (`claude -p`) and **consumes your Claude subscription usage** — you'll be asked to confirm once, and nothing runs before you do. Calls only happen when a *new* question arrives (an agent is already blocked on you), are capped at 2 at a time, and use a cheap model.

Turn this off to run Triage fully offline on lexical matching alone — it still works, just misses paraphrases.

mas.triage.ai.model.description: Model used for Triage's matching calls. A cheap, fast model is the right choice — these are short yes/no judgments.

mas.triage.conflict.detect.description: Raise a Triage item when two live sessions are editing the same file, so a collision surfaces before merge time. Local-only; never auto-answered.

mas.triage.defaultScope.description: Scope pre-selected when you answer. Most engineering decisions are repo-wide and long-lived, so this defaults wide; revoke is the backstop.

mas.triage.hold.enabled.markdownDescription:
Hold — suspend an agent inside its `AskUserQuestion` call until you answer in the Triage inbox, instead of it prompting in its own terminal. A held agent burns no tokens and does no speculative work.

Requires **Configure Claude Code Hooks**; re-run it after changing this. If the extension isn't running or the hold expires, Claude Code prompts exactly as it does today — a hold can only ever delay a prompt, never lose it.

mas.triage.hold.timeoutSeconds.description: How long a held question may wait for you before the agent falls back to prompting in its own terminal.

mas.attentionRouter.enabled.markdownDescription:
Attention Router — AI triage of which agent needs you, shown as a 'Needs you' inbox.

⚠️ Runs Claude Code in the background (`claude -p`) and **consumes your Claude subscription usage**. You'll be asked to confirm before the first run.

mas.mergeAdvisor.enabled.markdownDescription:
Merge Advisor — adds a command/toolbar button to rank multiple agents' diffs and recommend which to merge.

⚠️ **Consumes your Claude subscription usage** when run. You'll be asked to confirm before the first run.

mas.insights.triageModel.description: Model used for the Attention Router triage pass (cheap/fast model recommended).

mas.insights.mergeModel.description: Model used for the Merge Advisor ranking (quality model recommended).

mas.notifications.enabled.description: Show a notification when an agent needs your input, finishes, or hits an error.

mas.notifications.sound.description: Play a short system chime alongside notifications (best-effort; silently skipped if no player is available).

mas.notifications.onWaiting.description: Notify when an agent is waiting for your input (permission prompt / question).

mas.notifications.onDone.description: Notify when an Agent View-spawned agent finishes its task.

mas.notifications.onError.description: Notify when an agent hits an error.

mas.race.defaultCount.description: Default number of agents to spawn in an Agent Race.

mas.fanout.maxConcurrent.description: Maximum number of fan-out agents running at once. Remaining tasks queue and start as earlier agents finish.

mas.fanout.useWorktree.description: Run each fan-out agent in its own isolated git worktree (recommended). Disable to run them in the current directory.

mas.statusBar.enabled.description: Show a Fleet Pulse heartbeat in the status bar (e.g. "2 running · 1 needs you"), so you can monitor agents even when the Agent View panel is closed. It turns the warning color when an agent needs you; click it to jump there.

mas.review.allowLand.markdownDescription: Review & Land — allow the panel's **Squash-merge** action to commit an agent's branch into your current branch. Off by default; review, request-changes, copy-merge, and Open PR still work. The merge is refused on a dirty working tree, reversible until you push, and never deletes branches.

mas.review.maxDiffFiles.description: Maximum number of changed files to open as side-by-side diffs when you click an agent's Diff in Review & Land.

mas.review.ghPath.description: Path to the GitHub CLI (gh) used by Review & Land's Open PR. When gh isn't available, Open PR pushes the branch and copies a compare link instead.

mas.unattended.enabled.markdownDescription: Unattended Fleet — governed auto-pilot for Agent View-spawned agents. New agents auto-accept edits (`--permission-mode acceptEdits`; **Bash still prompts**), agents that stall mid-plan get nudged to continue, and an estimated cost meter shows in Fleet Pulse. Off by default.

mas.unattended.autoAcceptEdits.description: While Unattended Fleet is on, spawn agents with --permission-mode acceptEdits so file edits don't block. Bash and other tools still prompt (and escalate to a notification). Turn off to keep full prompting.

mas.unattended.nudgeStuckAfterSeconds.description: How long a managed agent may sit idle mid-plan before Unattended Fleet nudges it to continue.

mas.unattended.maxNudges.description: Maximum consecutive nudges before Unattended Fleet stops and escalates a stuck agent to you.

mas.unattended.maxCostUsd.description: Per-agent estimated-cost cap in USD. When a managed agent's estimated token cost passes this, Unattended Fleet pauses it (stops the run; its branch and diff are kept). 0 disables the cap.

mas.unattended.pricing.markdownDescription: Override the per-million-token prices used for the cost estimate. Keys `opus` / `sonnet` / `haiku` / `fable`, each `{ input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite }` in USD per 1M tokens (`cacheWrite` is the 5-minute write; 1-hour writes bill at 2x input). Leave empty to use list prices per model, which match Claude Code's own `/cost` — e.g. Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Fable 5.1 $10/$50, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5. Set it only for negotiated rates.

mas.evidence.enabled.markdownDescription: Evidence Gates — when a managed agent finishes working, run the project's checks (typecheck / lint / test, auto-detected) inside its worktree and show the result as a `checks` chip. Auto-detected commands ask for one-time per-repo approval before ever running. Only affects agents Agent View spawned.

mas.evidence.commands.markdownDescription: Explicit evidence commands to run in the agent's worktree (in order), e.g. `["npm run typecheck", "npm test"]`. When set, these replace auto-detection and skip the per-repo approval prompt.

mas.evidence.timeoutSeconds.description: Per-command timeout for evidence checks. A timed-out command counts as failed.

mas.evidence.maxConcurrent.description: How many agents' evidence checks may run at the same time; the rest queue.

mas.evidence.blockLandOnRed.markdownDescription: Block Review & Land's squash-merge when evidence is missing, failing, stale, or still running. Off = the land confirmation shows the evidence status but lets you proceed.

mas.evidence.selfRepair.markdownDescription: When evidence checks fail, send the failing output back to the agent's terminal so it can fix and re-verify — capped by `mas.evidence.maxRepairs`, then escalated to you. Off by default.

mas.evidence.maxRepairs.description: Maximum consecutive self-repair rounds per agent before Evidence Gates stops and escalates to you.

mas.presence.enabled.description: Live presence — badge files in the Explorer while an agent is editing them right now (hook-driven, fades after 45s of inactivity). Requires Configure Claude Code Hooks.

mas.shiftReport.aiNarrative.markdownDescription: Open the Fleet Shift Report with a short AI-written briefing on top of the table (uses `claude -p`, consumes subscription usage, consent-gated). Off by default, like every AI helper; the deterministic table needs no AI.

scripts.build: npm run build:webview && npm run build:ext
scripts.build:webview: cd webview-ui && npm install --no-audit --no-fund && npm run build
